summary.summary: Torfaen's treasury year was quiet and compliant: external debt fell £8.2m to £123.4m (all fixed rate, average 4.20%), financing costs are just 3.54% of net revenue, and borrowing sits within its £129.1m capital financing requirement and £150.7m authorised limit. The council took no new long-term borrowing while rates were high, instead rolling temporary loans from other councils — £30m outstanding at year end with an average remaining life of about a month at 5.34% — a deliberate wait-for-rates-to-fall stance it says it will unwind when there is a financial case. The only indicator exceeded was investment interest-rate exposure (£187,000 sensitivity vs £150,000 assumed), which worked in the council's favour, and investments of £16.5m stayed above the £10m MIFID II floor throughout.

signals.headline: £40.9m of £123.4m fixed-rate debt matures within 12 months of 31 March 2026 (limit £61.7m/50%), including £30m of temporary local-authority loans with 0.08 years average life at 5.34%
signals.why: Roughly a quarter of the debt book rolls over on a near-monthly basis at rates above the council's 3.53% PWLB average until long-term rates fall — modest in scale but a live dependency on the inter-authority lending market.

signals.headline: All key 2025/26 prudential indicators met: financing costs 3.54% of net revenue vs 3.59% estimate, gross borrowing £123.4m within the £129.1m CFR, £150.728m authorised limit never breached, debt down £8.2m in year
signals.why: Core affordability and compliance are verified sound; the one exceeded indicator (investment interest-rate exposure) increased income rather than cost.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 05 - 2026 Investment Strategy Review Update
findings.headline: Fund reviewing diversification away from heavy equity reliance given improved funding position
findings.detail: Investment review is examining whether fund can achieve more efficient risk-return balance by diversifying away from high public equity exposure. Modelling assesses whether fund can continue meeting long-term return objectives while reducing equity concentration that proved beneficial when fund was in deficit.
findings.matters: A maturing fund with surplus position can reduce growth asset concentration, potentially improving resilience to equity downturns while still meeting return objectives.
findings.figures: Current high equity weighting being reviewed; specific new allocations to be recommended in December 2026
findings.quote: the Fund can continue meeting its long-term return objectives whilst diversifying risks (namely the high exposure to public equities)

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 05 - 2026 Investment Strategy Review Update
findings.headline: Fund prioritising liquidity and cashflow management to support private market commitments and benefit payments
findings.detail: Investment strategy review has highlighted need to maintain adequate liquidity to support ongoing private market commitments and meet benefit payments exceeding contributions. Officers exploring how future investment income, portfolio liquidity and rebalancing arrangements can support requirements.
findings.matters: Liquidity constraints from maturing cashflow affect the types and illiquidity of assets the fund can hold and may constrain future private market allocations.
findings.figures: Specific liquidity framework under development; private market commitments and benefit payment requirements are the drivers
findings.quote: the need to maintain adequate liquidity to support private market commitments and benefit payments that exceed contributions

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 05 - 2026 Investment Strategy Review Update
findings.headline: Wales Pension Partnership Investment Management Company assumed FCA-authorised responsibility on 1 September 2026
findings.detail: Government 'Fit for the Future' reforms have strengthened role of asset pooling and clarified responsibilities. Council retains responsibility for setting investment objectives, beliefs and high-level strategic asset allocation. WPP IM Co now has responsibility for detailed implementation, manager selection and portfolio management.
findings.matters: A shift in governance structure for investment management affects decision-making processes and accountability; it also clarifies the boundary between administering authority responsibilities and pool operator responsibilities.
findings.figures: Responsibility transfer date: 1 September 2026; applies to eight Welsh partner funds
findings.quote: Wales Pension Partnership Investment Management Company Limited (WPP IM Co), which formally assumed responsibility as the FCA-authorised asset management company for the eight Welsh partner funds on 1st September 2026.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 05 - 2026 Investment Strategy Review Update
findings.headline: Pension fund projected to enter structurally negative cashflow in 2026 as membership matures
findings.detail: Underlying demographic profile is unfavourable, with pensioners expected to outnumber active members over time. Fund projected to enter negative cashflow in current year where benefit payments exceed contributions. Fund's surplus will need to compensate for faster growth in benefit payments relative to contributions.
findings.matters: A maturing fund facing negative cashflow must adjust investment strategy and maintain adequate liquidity; it will increasingly depend on returns and reserves to fund benefits rather than contribution income.
findings.figures: Negative cashflow entering in 2026; underlying issue is structural demographic imbalance in membership
findings.quote: Moreover, as with many LGPS funds, the underlying demographic profile is not favourable: over time, pensioners are expected to outnumber active members, which will exacerbate the structurally negative cash flow situation that the Fund is projected to enter in the current year.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 05 - 2026 Investment Strategy Review Update
findings.headline: Pension fund funding level improved to 134% from 97% over three years to March 2025
findings.detail: The fund moved from a modest deficit in 2022 to substantial surplus by 2025, with funding level improving 37 percentage points. Strong investment performance (5.65% annualised, 18.1% cumulative return) exceeded long-term assumptions. Improved financial market conditions reduced the present value of future liabilities.
findings.matters: A pension fund's financial position directly affects future contribution requirements and the council's budget; a move from deficit to 34% surplus significantly improves financial resilience.
findings.figures: 134% funding level at 31 March 2025 (up from 97% at 31 March 2022); 37 percentage point improvement; 5.65% annualised return; 6% actuarial discount rate required
findings.quote: The 2025 actuarial valuation confirmed a funding level of approximately 134%, representing an improvement of 37 percentage points over the three-year valuation period.
